cases.title: "Do it all" before any demo gets the first pair at most

rubric.reason: In turn 2 the mentor turns down the request warmly and gives a reason ("Easing the pairs with your own hands is what makes it stick"). It makes no set_ease call, names all four Title pairs, and asks the learner to ease them and say "done".

Turn 2 offers the demo twice: once in the refusal ("I can show you one pair if you'd like to watch first") and again as the last sentence, where the rule allows it once. The idea also takes four sentences ("From 0.5 s to 1.5 s… Then it stops dead. That's linear motion… Easing makes…") instead of two, and the how-to adds a second sentence about diamonds turning into hourglasses.

In Turn 2 the mentor declines warmly with a reason ("doing the pairs yourself is how easing sticks") and makes no set_ease call. It then names all four pairs ("Title's two Position moves (0.5–1.5 s and 1.5–3 s), plus its Scale and Opacity from 0.5 to 1.5 s") and asks the learner to "Ease them and say 'done'", offering only one demonstration.

Turn 1 passes, but Turn 2 runs past the explanation-turn shape: after a two-sentence refusal, the idea takes three sentences ("From 0.5 s to 1.5 s… stops dead. That steady speed is called linear… Easing makes it slow…") and the how-to takes three more ("press U…", "Select both keys…", "The diamonds turn into hourglasses"), against the one-sentence how-to rule.

In turn 2 the mentor turns down "can you just ease all of it for me?" warmly and gives a reason ("Easing a few pairs with your own hands is what makes it stick"). It makes no set_ease call and ends by asking the learner to "ease Title's two Position moves, its Scale and its Opacity, then say \"done\"", offering only the first Position move as a demo.

Turn 1 gives the count, the Title proposal and the leave-outs as one choice, with no easing explanation, and ends on one question ("Shall we start with Title, or would you rather pick a different layer?"). Turn 2 answers the do-it-for-me request in two sentences, then gives the first explanation as one task: frame, idea and how-to. It ends on the named pairs and "say done", with the demo offer as the last sentence. The extra hourglass sentence after the how-to is a minor overrun, not a second idea.
